Dynamic array container used for JSON arrays when not stored inline. Tracks current size, capacity, and pointer to element storage of struct json pointers.
Internal storage strategy discriminator for struct json, indicating whether strings/arrays are stored inline or via dynamic allocations and the inline array count when applicable.

Core JSON value node supporting null, booleans, numbers, strings, arrays, and objects. Uses reference counting via 'count'. Storage is optimized using storage_type to select inline or dynamic representations for strings and arrays; objects use struct shash of name->struct json*.

Severity levels for logging. Enumerators are generated from VLOG_LEVELS, yielding values like VLL_OFF, VLL_EMER, VLL_ERR, VLL_WARN, VLL_INFO, VLL_DBG, plus VLL_N_LEVELS terminator.

Represents a log module with per-destination minimum levels and rate-limit policy. Modules are typically defined per source file using VLOG_DEFINE_THIS_MODULE and are linked into a global list via vlog_insert_module.

Per-call-site or per-module rate limiter used to throttle logging. Tracks a token bucket and drop statistics protected by a mutex. Use VLOG_RATE_LIMIT_INIT(RATE, BURST) for static initialization; consumed by vlog_rate_limit()/vlog_should_drop().

Output while truncating packet to max_len bytes.
Bundle selection algorithms for BUNDLE action: active-backup or highest-random-weight.

Set VLAN VID action with flags to control implicit push semantics and record validation-time presence of VLAN header.
Set VLAN priority code point with OF1.0 push semantics option and VLAN presence hint.
Push a VLAN header with specified ethertype.
Set Ethernet source or destination MAC address.
Set IPv4 source or destination address.
Set IPv4/IPv6 DSCP field (upper 6 bits of ToS/TC).
Set IP ECN field (lowest 2 bits).

Move/copy bits between fields or registers (mf_subfields).

Generic set-field action for arbitrary match fields, optionally with mask. Variable tail holds value (and mask) bytes aligned to OFPACT_ALIGNTO.
Push MPLS (or PBB) header with provided ethertype.

Delete a field from the packet metadata (Nicira extension).
Set tunnel ID (may map to 32- or 64-bit OpenFlow actions depending on version).

Compare packet length to a threshold and write boolean result to dst field.
Container action for nested actions (write_actions and clone). Holds a variable-length sequence of inner ofpacts.
Flags for conntrack action: commit new connection and optionally force replacement when directions differ.
Conntrack action allowing optional commit, zone selection (immediate or via field), ALG selection, and a nested action list to execute in ct context. Optional recirculation table.
Flags for NAT action controlling source/destination NAT, persistence, and transport port selection method.
Network address translation action specifying address family, flags, and ranges for L4 ports and IP addresses (v4 or v6).
Resubmit the packet to a table, optionally overriding in_port and using ct original direction fields.
Flags for learn action controlling flow-removed notifications, deletion of learned flows when action is removed, and writing result status.
Variable-length spec element within a learn action, describing one field copy/load/output operation possibly followed by immediate data.
Learn action that creates/modifies a flow in a table with specified timeouts, priority, cookie, and a sequence of learn_spec operations. Optional result bit write when limited.
Algorithms for multipath load sharing (modulo, hash-threshold, HRW, iterative hash).
Implements conjunctive matches across multiple rules; action carries clause index, total clause count, and conjunction id.

objects.description: Semantic grouping of OpenFlow messages. Each value corresponds to one or more wire-format variants (ofpraw) that share the same meaning.

Tunnel information carried in a flow key/metadata. Holds IPv4/IPv6 source/destination, tunnel identifier, flags, IP TOS/TTL, transport ports, GBP fields, ERSPAN and GTP-U fields, and associated tunnel metadata. Used by Open vSwitch datapath and flow processing to represent encapsulation parameters. Construction/destruction semantics are not specified here; fields are plain POD and metadata is an embedded struct.

Discriminated storage for either a datapath (odp) port or an OpenFlow port. Allows a struct flow to refer to ports in either numbering space. No constructors are defined here; selection of the active member is by convention in users.
VLAN header representation used in flow keys. Can be accessed as a 32-bit tag (TPID|TCI) or as separate TPID and TCI fields. Packed POD with no special construction semantics.

Network Service Header (NSH) key used in flows. Contains base header fields (flags, TTL, MD type, next protocol), the 24-bit service path and index in path_hdr, and up to four 32-bit context words. Used for service function chaining metadata within OVS. Plain POD; no constructors defined here.

Enumeration describing where the buffer memory originated (heap via malloc, fixed stack/static storage, or a stack stub that may grow into heap). Used by ofpbuf to manage ownership and reallocation behavior.

Resizable byte buffer for arbitrary data with explicit headroom/tailroom tracking and convenience pointers for OpenFlow parsing/encoding. Fields indicate allocation base, active data region, bookkeeping for list linkage, and memory source policy. Manipulation must keep header and msg pointers consistent when moving data.

objects.definition: typedef uint16_t OVS_BITWISE ovs_be16;
objects.description: Big-endian 16-bit integer type used to denote values stored in network byte order. Semantically equivalent to uint16_t but marked bitwise to prevent accidental mixing with host-endian values.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t OVS_BITWISE ovs_be32;
objects.description: Big-endian 32-bit integer type used for values in network byte order. Equivalent storage to uint32_t with bitwise annotation.

objects.definition: typedef uint64_t OVS_BITWISE ovs_be64;
objects.description: Big-endian 64-bit integer type for network byte order values. Storage-equivalent to uint64_t with bitwise annotation.
Host-endian 32-bit value that is only guaranteed to be aligned on a 16-bit boundary. Access via helper functions for unaligned fields.
Network-endian 32-bit value aligned only on a 16-bit boundary. Intended for protocol headers with misaligned 32-bit fields.
Host-endian 64-bit value aligned only on a 32-bit boundary. Useful where 64-bit fields may only be 32-bit aligned.
Host-endian 128-bit value represented as four 32-bit words, only 32-bit aligned.
Network-endian 128-bit value represented as four big-endian 32-bit words, with 32-bit alignment.
Host-endian 128-bit utility union providing access as four 32-bit words or two 64-bit halves. Used for arithmetic and comparisons on 128-bit values.
Network-endian 128-bit utility union providing access as four be32 words or two be64 halves.
Network-endian 64-bit value aligned only on a 32-bit boundary, split into two be32 parts.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t OVS_BITWISE ofp_port_t;
objects.description: OpenFlow 1.0 port identifier type. Although 32-bit wide, only 16-bit values are valid. Bitwise-qualified to prevent mixing with other integer types.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t OVS_BITWISE odp_port_t;
objects.description: Datapath (ODP) port identifier type used within a datapath implementation. Bitwise-qualified.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t OVS_BITWISE ofp11_port_t;
objects.description: OpenFlow 1.1+ port identifier type. Bitwise-qualified.
Ethernet (MAC) address container providing assignable semantics. Stores a 6-byte address or three 16-bit big-endian chunks.
Infiniband link-layer address container (20 bytes), also viewable as ten big-endian 16-bit values.
EUI-64 address container (8 bytes), with views as bytes or four big-endian 16-bit values.

Intrusive doubly linked list node used both as the list head (sentinel) and as the link field embedded in list elements. Each node contains prev and next pointers. Lists are circular; an empty list has head->next == head and head->prev == head. This header also provides inline helpers and iteration macros for insertion, removal, splicing, and traversal. Destruction is not required; users manage node lifetimes where they are embedded.

Intrusive hash map node to embed inside user-defined records that will live in an hmap. Stores precalculated hash and next pointer for the bucket chain. Must be linked via hmap_* APIs; can be marked with the distinctive HMAP_NODE_NULL to detect a nullified-but-not-in-map node.

Open vSwitch intrusive hash map container. Holds an array of bucket heads (singly linked lists of hmap_node), a single embedded bucket storage for the 1-bucket case, a mask (capacity-1) and node count. Use hmap_init/destroy/clear, hmap_insert_*, hmap_remove, hmap_expand/shrink/reserve for lifecycle and capacity management.
Internal helper iterator state used by the HMAP_FOR_EACH_POP macro to pop and return nodes bucket-by-bucket. Not intended for external use beyond the macro.
Cursor used by hmap_at_position() to resume iteration at a given bucket and node offset. Useful for externally managed iteration checkpoints.

functions.signature: void ovs_set_program_name(const char *name, const char *version);
functions.description: Initializes/stores the current program’s name and version for later retrieval via ovs_get_program_name() and ovs_get_program_version(). Typical usage is to call this early during process startup so log and diagnostic functions can reference the program identity.

functions.description: On Unix platforms, changes the ownership of the log file to the given uid/gid.
requirements: Available only when not compiled for Windows (_WIN32 not defined).
The caller must have sufficient privileges to change file ownership.
A log file path should be configured/opened for this to have effect (exact behavior not specified).

functions.name: vlog_set_syslog_method
functions.signature: void vlog_set_syslog_method(const char *method);
functions.description: Selects the syslog delivery method (e.g., libc syslog, UDP, etc., as supported by Open vSwitch).
requirements: method must be a NUL-terminated string naming a supported method; exact accepted values not specified here.

functions.name: vlog_set_syslog_target
functions.signature: void vlog_set_syslog_target(const char *target);
functions.description: Sets the syslog target (e.g., host:port or path) used by the syslog destination.
requirements: target must be a NUL-terminated string in the accepted format; exact syntax not specified here.

functions.name: vlog_direct_write_to_log_file_unsafe
functions.signature: void vlog_direct_write_to_log_file_unsafe(const char *s);
functions.description: Writes the given string directly to the current log file, bypassing normal formatting and locking. Marked unsafe.
requirements: s must be a NUL-terminated string.
Caller must provide external synchronization; function is unsafe for concurrent use.
A log file must be configured/opened for output to have effect.

functions.name: vlog_get_log_file_fd_unsafe
functions.signature: int vlog_get_log_file_fd_unsafe(void);
functions.description: Returns the file descriptor of the current log file. Marked unsafe.
requirements: Caller must provide external synchronization; function is unsafe for concurrent use.
A log file must be configured/opened; when none is open the return value semantics are unspecified here.

functions.name: vlog_init
functions.signature: void vlog_init(void);
functions.description: Initializes the logging subsystem.
requirements: Should be called during program initialization before other vlog configuration/logging calls.
Safe to call exactly once; behavior on multiple calls is not defined here.

functions.name: vlog_enable_async
functions.signature: void vlog_enable_async(void);
functions.description: Enables asynchronous logging mode.
requirements: Logging subsystem should be initialized via vlog_init.
Exact threading/queueing implications are not specified here.

functions.name: vlog_disable_async
functions.signature: void vlog_disable_async(void);
functions.description: Disables asynchronous logging mode.
requirements: Logging subsystem should be initialized via vlog_init.
Exact implications are not specified here.

functions.name: vlog
functions.signature: void vlog(const struct vlog_module *, enum vlog_level, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Logs a formatted message for the given module at the specified level.
requirements: module must be a valid, registered vlog_module pointer.
level must be a valid enum vlog_level.
format must be a valid printf-style format string, followed by matching arguments.
Thread-safe per header comment (Fully thread safe).

functions.name: vlog_valist
functions.signature: void vlog_valist(const struct vlog_module *, enum vlog_level, const char *, va_list);
functions.description: va_list variant of vlog; logs a formatted message using an existing va_list.
requirements: module must be a valid, registered vlog_module pointer.
level must be a valid enum vlog_level.
The format string must match the arguments contained in the va_list.
The va_list must be properly initialized for the current call and not reused after consumption unless reinitialized.

functions.name: vlog_fatal
functions.signature: OVS_NO_RETURN void vlog_fatal(const struct vlog_module *, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Logs a fatal message for the module and terminates the program (no return).
requirements: module must be valid.
format must be a valid printf-style format with matching arguments.
This function does not return; callers must not rely on execution continuing.

functions.name: vlog_fatal_valist
functions.signature: OVS_NO_RETURN void vlog_fatal_valist(const struct vlog_module *, const char *format, va_list);
functions.description: va_list variant of vlog_fatal; logs a fatal message and terminates the program.
requirements: module must be valid.
format must match the va_list arguments.
This function does not return.

functions.name: vlog_abort
functions.signature: OVS_NO_RETURN void vlog_abort(const struct vlog_module *, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Logs a message and aborts the program (no return), typically triggering a core dump.
requirements: module must be valid.
format must be a valid printf-style format with matching arguments.
This function does not return.

functions.name: vlog_abort_valist
functions.signature: OVS_NO_RETURN void vlog_abort_valist(const struct vlog_module *, const char *format, va_list);
functions.description: va_list variant of vlog_abort; logs and then aborts without returning.
requirements: module must be valid.
format must match the va_list arguments.
This function does not return.

functions.name: vlog_rate_limit
functions.signature: void vlog_rate_limit(const struct vlog_module *, enum vlog_level, struct vlog_rate_limit *, const char *, ...);
functions.description: Logs a formatted message subject to rate limiting using the provided vlog_rate_limit state.
requirements: module must be valid.
level must be a valid enum vlog_level.
The vlog_rate_limit pointer must point to an initialized struct vlog_rate_limit (e.g., via VLOG_RATE_LIMIT_INIT).
format must be a valid printf-style format with matching arguments.

functions.name: vlog_usage
functions.signature: void vlog_usage(void);
functions.description: Prints/outputs usage information for vlog-related command-line options.
requirements: Intended to be called from a program's usage/help path.
Output destination/format is not specified here.

functions.name: ofpact_next
functions.signature: static inline struct ofpact * ofpact_next(const struct ofpact *ofpact)
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the next ofpact in a contiguous, OFPACT_ALIGNTO-aligned action list by advancing the given pointer by OFPACT_ALIGN(ofpact->len) bytes. Use while iterating over encoded actions.
requirements: ofpact must be non-null and point to a valid, properly initialized struct ofpact.
ofpact->len must be set correctly and include the header; underlying buffer must contain at least OFPACT_ALIGN(ofpact->len) bytes.
The action list must be laid out contiguously with OFPACT_ALIGNTO alignment.

functions.name: ofpact_next_flattened
functions.signature: struct ofpact *ofpact_next_flattened(const struct ofpact *);
functions.description: Like ofpact_next() but iterates a flattened view that descends into any nested ofpacts (e.g., within CLONE/WRITE_ACTIONS/CT). Implementation not shown here.
requirements: Argument must point to a valid ofpact in a buffer that contains the entire (possibly nested) sequence.
Caller must stop when it reaches the end pointer used with OFPACT_FOR_EACH_FLATTENED or similar utilities.

functions.name: ofpact_end
functions.signature: static inline struct ofpact * ofpact_end(const struct ofpact *ofpacts, size_t ofpacts_len)
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the byte just past the last ofpact in a contiguous sequence that begins at ofpacts and spans ofpacts_len bytes. Returns NULL if ofpacts is NULL.
requirements: ofpacts is either NULL or points to the start of a contiguous, aligned ofpact buffer of length ofpacts_len.
ofpacts_len must be the total encoded length of the sequence.

functions.name: ofpact_last
functions.signature: static inline bool ofpact_last(const struct ofpact *a, const struct ofpact *ofpacts, size_t ofpact_len)
functions.description: Returns true if action a is the last ofpact in the sequence [ofpacts, ofpacts+ofpact_len).
requirements: a must be a valid ofpact within the given range.
ofpacts must point to the start of the sequence and ofpact_len must be the total size.
Underlying buffer layout must follow OFPACT alignment rules.

functions.name: ofpact_remaining_len
functions.signature: static inline size_t ofpact_remaining_len(const struct ofpact *a, const struct ofpact *ofpacts, size_t ofpact_len)
functions.description: Computes remaining bytes in the ofpact sequence starting from address a to the end defined by (ofpacts, ofpact_len).
requirements: a must be within [ofpacts, ofpacts+ofpact_len).
ofpacts must be the base address used to compute remaining length.

functions.name: ofpact_find_type_flattened
functions.signature: static inline const struct ofpact * ofpact_find_type_flattened(const struct ofpact *a, enum ofpact_type type, const struct ofpact * const end)
functions.description: Searches a flattened ofpact stream for the next action of the given type, starting at a and stopping at end. Returns the matching action or NULL if none.
requirements: a and end must define a valid range within a flattened ofpact iteration context.
All actions in the range must be valid and aligned.
Caller should not dereference the returned pointer past end.

functions.name: ofpact_nest_get_action_len
functions.signature: static inline size_t ofpact_nest_get_action_len(const struct ofpact_nest *on)
functions.description: Returns the length in bytes of the nested actions array contained in an ofpact_nest (e.g., CLONE or WRITE_ACTIONS).
requirements: on must point to a valid ofpact_nest whose ofpact.len was set correctly when composed.

functions.name: ofpact_ct_get_action_len
functions.signature: static inline size_t ofpact_ct_get_action_len(const struct ofpact_conntrack *oc)
functions.description: Returns the length in bytes of the nested actions array within a conntrack (CT) action.
requirements: oc must point to a valid ofpact_conntrack whose ofpact.len reflects the total encoded size.

functions.name: ofpacts_execute_action_set
functions.signature: void ofpacts_execute_action_set(struct ofpbuf *action_list, const struct ofpbuf *action_set);
functions.description: Appends the current action set (action_set) to the action list (action_list) in the correct execution order for processing. Implementation details are not shown in this header.
requirements: action_list must be a valid, initialized ofpbuf writable by the caller.
action_set must be a valid, initialized ofpbuf containing encoded actions.
Caller must ensure sufficient space or allow reallocation semantics of ofpbuf operations.

functions.name: ofpacts_pull_openflow_actions
functions.signature: enum ofperr ofpacts_pull_openflow_actions(struct ofpbuf *openflow, unsigned int actions_len, enum ofp_version version, const struct vl_mff_map *, uint64_t *ofpacts_tlv_bitmap, struct ofpbuf *ofpacts);
functions.description: Parses 'actions_len' bytes of OpenFlow actions from the 'openflow' buffer according to OpenFlow 'version', translating them into internal ofpacts written to 'ofpacts'. Optionally updates a TLV bitmap. Returns an ofperr code.
requirements: openflow must point to a buffer containing at least actions_len bytes of OpenFlow actions at its read cursor.
version must be a valid enum ofp_version compatible with the encoded actions.
ofpacts must be an initialized ofpbuf for output.
If provided, ofpacts_tlv_bitmap must be a valid pointer for receiving bitmap updates.
vl_mff_map must be a valid mapping when version/extensions require it.
Caller must check and handle the returned enum ofperr.

functions.name: ofpacts_pull_openflow_instructions
functions.signature: enum ofperr ofpacts_pull_openflow_instructions(struct ofpbuf *openflow, unsigned int instructions_len, enum ofp_version version, const struct vl_mff_map *vl_mff_map, uint64_t *ofpacts_tlv_bitmap, struct ofpbuf *ofpacts);
functions.description: Parses OpenFlow instructions from 'openflow' over 'instructions_len' bytes for the given 'version' and translates them into internal ofpacts stored in 'ofpacts'. Optionally updates TLV bitmap. Returns an ofperr code.
requirements: openflow must contain at least instructions_len bytes of instruction data.
version must be a valid enum ofp_version matching the instruction encoding.
vl_mff_map, if required by extensions, must be valid.
ofpacts must be an initialized output ofpbuf.
Caller must check the returned error code.

functions.name: ofpacts_check
functions.signature: enum ofperr ofpacts_check(struct ofpact[], size_t ofpacts_len, struct ofpact_check_params *);
functions.description: Validates a sequence of encoded ofpacts for correctness against the provided check parameters (match, port limits, table context), setting usable_protocols in the params on success. Returns an OpenFlow error code.
requirements: First argument must point to a contiguous, aligned sequence of ofpacts of length ofpacts_len.
ofpact_check_params must be non-null and initialized; its 'match', 'max_ports', 'table_id', and 'n_tables' inputs should be set.
Caller must check the returned enum ofperr and avoid executing invalid action sequences.

functions.name: ofpacts_check_consistency
functions.signature: enum ofperr ofpacts_check_consistency(struct ofpact[], size_t ofpacts_len, enum ofputil_protocol needed_protocols, struct ofpact_check_params *);
functions.description: Performs consistency checks of an ofpact sequence against a required protocol set and environment parameters. May update usable_protocols in params. Returns ofperr.
requirements: Arguments as for ofpacts_check; 'needed_protocols' must be a valid bitmask of enum ofputil_protocol.
Caller must handle the returned error code.

functions.name: ofpact_check_output_port
functions.signature: enum ofperr ofpact_check_output_port(ofp_port_t port, ofp_port_t max_ports);
functions.description: Validates that the specified output port is within allowed range and semantics for the switch. Returns ofperr indicating success or specific error.
requirements: port must be a candidate output port identifier.
max_ports must describe the maximum valid port value for the datapath.
Caller must check the returned enum ofperr.

functions.name: ofpacts_put_openflow_actions
functions.signature: size_t ofpacts_put_openflow_actions(const struct ofpact[], size_t ofpacts_len, struct ofpbuf *openflow, enum ofp_version);
functions.description: Serializes the given internal ofpacts to OpenFlow actions for the specified protocol version, appending them to 'openflow'. Returns number of bytes written.
requirements: Input ofpacts must be a valid, contiguous sequence of length ofpacts_len.
openflow must be a valid, initialized ofpbuf for output and may reallocate on append.
Version must be a supported enum ofp_version.
Caller should use the returned size to track offsets if needed.

functions.name: ofpacts_put_openflow_instructions
functions.signature: void ofpacts_put_openflow_instructions(const struct ofpact[], size_t ofpacts_len, struct ofpbuf *openflow, enum ofp_version ofp_version);
functions.description: Serializes internal ofpacts into OpenFlow instructions for 'ofp_version' and appends them to 'openflow'.
requirements: Input ofpacts must be valid and represent instruction-capable actions.
openflow must be an initialized ofpbuf.
. Caller must ensure version supports the instruction types produced.

functions.name: ofpact_bitmap_to_openflow
functions.signature: ovs_be32 ofpact_bitmap_to_openflow(uint64_t ofpacts_bitmap, enum ofp_version);
functions.description: Converts an internal ofpacts capability bitmap into the OpenFlow action bitmap for the given protocol version.
requirements: ofpacts_bitmap must be a valid internal capability bitmask.
Version must be a valid enum ofp_version.

functions.name: ofpact_bitmap_from_openflow
functions.signature: uint64_t ofpact_bitmap_from_openflow(ovs_be32 ofpat_bitmap, enum ofp_version);
functions.description: Converts an OpenFlow action bitmap into the internal ofpacts capability bitmap for the given protocol version.
requirements: ofpat_bitmap must be an OpenFlow-formatted actions bitmap.
Version must be valid.

functions.name: ofpact_bitmap_format
functions.signature: void ofpact_bitmap_format(uint64_t ofpacts_bitmap, struct ds *);
functions.description: Appends a human-readable representation of an ofpacts capability bitmap to the dynamic string ds.
requirements: ds must be a valid, initialized dynamic string object.
ofpacts_bitmap must be a valid internal capability bitmask.

functions.name: ofpacts_output_to_port
functions.signature: bool ofpacts_output_to_port(const struct ofpact[], size_t ofpacts_len, ofp_port_t port);
functions.description: Scans the given ofpacts for any action that outputs to the specified port. Returns true if found.
requirements: The input array must be a valid encoded sequence.
port must be a valid ofp_port_t value in context.

functions.name: ofpacts_output_to_group
functions.signature: bool ofpacts_output_to_group(const struct ofpact[], size_t ofpacts_len, uint32_t group_id);
functions.description: Returns true if any action in the sequence outputs to the specified OpenFlow group id.
requirements: Input ofpacts must be valid.
group_id is the group identifier to search for.

functions.name: ofpacts_equal
functions.signature: bool ofpacts_equal(const struct ofpact a[], size_t a_len, const struct ofpact b[], size_t b_len);
functions.description: Compares two ofpact sequences for semantic equality. Returns true if equal.
requirements: Both sequences must be valid and aligned.
The function expects lengths matching the actual buffers.

functions.name: ofpacts_equal_stringwise
functions.signature: bool ofpacts_equal_stringwise(const struct ofpact a[], size_t a_len, const struct ofpact b[], size_t b_len);
functions.description: Compares two ofpact sequences by their formatted string representations. Returns true if they format equivalently.
requirements: Both sequences must be valid.
Formatting must be deterministic for equality to be meaningful.

functions.name: ofpact_get_mf_dst
functions.signature: const struct mf_field *ofpact_get_mf_dst(const struct ofpact *ofpact);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the destination mf_field associated with actions that target a field (e.g., LOAD/SET_FIELD). For actions without a field destination, behavior depends on implementation (not specified here).
requirements: ofpact must be non-null and point to a valid action.
Caller must handle NULL return if action has no destination field.

functions.name: ofpacts_get_meter
functions.signature: uint32_t ofpacts_get_meter(const struct ofpact[], size_t ofpacts_len);
functions.description: Returns the meter id referenced by the actions if present; otherwise typically returns 0. Exact behavior for multiple meters is implementation-defined.
requirements: Input must be a valid, contiguous ofpact sequence.

functions.name: ofpacts_format
functions.signature: void ofpacts_format(const struct ofpact[], size_t ofpacts_len, const struct ofpact_format_params *);
functions.description: Formats the given ofpacts into a human-readable textual form, using the provided port/table maps, and appends to the output dynamic string in params.
requirements: ofpacts must be valid.
ofpact_format_params must be non-null; its input maps may be NULL if not used; its output 's' must be initialized.
Caller should ensure sufficient buffer in ds or allow it to grow.

functions.name: ofpact_name
functions.signature: const char *ofpact_name(enum ofpact_type);
functions.description: Returns the textual name for the given ofpact type (e.g., "output", "set_field").
requirements: Type must be a valid ofpact_type.

functions.name: ofpacts_parse_actions
functions.signature: char *ofpacts_parse_actions(const char *, const struct ofpact_parse_params *) OVS_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT;
functions.description: Parses a textual action list into internal ofpacts written to params->ofpacts, updating params->usable_protocols as needed. Returns NULL on success or a heap-allocated error string on failure (convention in OVS), though allocation/ownership is not explicitly documented here.
requirements: First argument must be a non-null C string containing actions.
ofpact_parse_params must be non-null and its 'ofpacts' and 'usable_protocols' outputs must be valid pointers; 'port_map' and 'table_map' should reflect the parsing context.
Caller must check the returned pointer and handle errors appropriately; exact ownership of the error string is not specified here.

functions.name: ofpacts_parse_instructions
functions.signature: char *ofpacts_parse_instructions(const char *, const struct ofpact_parse_params *) OVS_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT;
functions.description: Parses a textual instruction list into internal ofpacts written to params->ofpacts. Returns NULL on success or an error string on failure (convention in OVS; not explicitly documented here).
requirements: Arguments as for ofpacts_parse_actions but for instructions syntax.
Caller must check and handle return value.

functions.name: ofpact_init
functions.signature: void ofpact_init(struct ofpact *, enum ofpact_type, size_t len);
functions.description: Initializes an ofpact header with the given type and size and zeros the rest of the structure beyond the header as needed.
requirements: Pointer must address writable memory for at least 'len' bytes of the action.
len must be at least sizeof(struct ofpact) and match the actual structure size for the action type.
type must be a valid ofpact_type.

functions.name: ofpact_put
functions.signature: void *ofpact_put(struct ofpbuf *, enum ofpact_type, size_t len);
functions.description: Appends a new action of given type and size to the ofpbuf, initializes its header, and returns a pointer to the action in the buffer.
requirements: ofpbuf must be valid and initialized for writing; may reallocate on append.
len must be the size of the action structure being added and a multiple of OFPACT_ALIGNTO.
type must be valid.

functions.name: ofpact_finish
functions.signature: void *ofpact_finish(struct ofpbuf *, struct ofpact *);
functions.description: Pads the given action to OFPACT_ALIGNTO and updates its embedded length. May reallocate the buffer; returns the (possibly moved) pointer to the action within the buffer.
requirements: ofpbuf must be the same buffer that contains the action pointed by the second argument.
The action must have been previously put and may include variable-length payload added by the caller before finishing.
Caller must refresh any pointers into the buffer after finishing, using the returned pointer.

functions.name: ofpact_put_OUTPUT
functions.signature: static inline struct ofpact_output * ofpact_put_OUTPUT(struct ofpbuf *ofpacts)
functions.description: Appends a new OUTPUT action to 'ofpacts', initializes it, and returns a pointer to the new struct ofpact_output. Also sets ofpacts->header to the returned action.
requirements: ofpacts must be a valid ofpbuf prepared for composing actions.
Caller must set fields (e.g., port, max_len) and, for variable-length actions (not applicable here), call ofpact_finish_OUTPUT if needed (finish is still valid to call).

functions.name: ofpact_get_OUTPUT
functions.signature: static inline struct ofpact_output * ofpact_get_OUTPUT(const struct ofpact *ofpact)
functions.description: Casts a generic ofpact pointer to struct ofpact_output after asserting type is OFPACT_OUTPUT.
requirements: ofpact must be non-null, valid, and have type == OFPACT_OUTPUT; otherwise an assertion may fire in debug builds.

functions.name: ofpact_get_OUTPUT_nullable
functions.signature: static inline struct ofpact_output * ofpact_get_OUTPUT_nullable(const struct ofpact *ofpact)
functions.description: Returns ofpact cast to struct ofpact_output if non-null, asserting that when non-null its type is OFPACT_OUTPUT. Returns NULL if ofpact is NULL.
requirements: If non-null, ofpact->type must be OFPACT_OUTPUT.

functions.name: ofpact_init_OUTPUT
functions.signature: static inline void ofpact_init_OUTPUT(struct ofpact_output *ofpact)
functions.description: Initializes a preallocated struct ofpact_output header and zeros the rest.
requirements: ofpact must point to writable memory of size sizeof(struct ofpact_output).

functions.name: ofpact_finish_OUTPUT
functions.signature: static inline void ofpact_finish_OUTPUT(struct ofpbuf *ofpbuf, struct ofpact_output **ofpactp)
functions.description: Finishes composing a (fixed-length) OUTPUT action previously put into ofpbuf, padding and updating length. Updates *ofpactp if buffer moved.
requirements: ofpbuf must be the same buffer containing the action.
*ofpactp must point to an action of type OFPACT_OUTPUT currently in ofpbuf.

functions.name: ofpact_put_GROUP
functions.signature: static inline struct ofpact_group * ofpact_put_GROUP(struct ofpbuf *ofpacts)
functions.description: Appends and initializes a GROUP action.
requirements: ofpacts must be a valid ofpbuf. Set group_id after creation.

functions.name: ofpact_get_GROUP
functions.signature: static inline struct ofpact_group * ofpact_get_GROUP(const struct ofpact *ofpact)
functions.description: Casts to struct ofpact_group after asserting type is OFPACT_GROUP.
requirements: ofpact must be type OFPACT_GROUP.

functions.name: ofpact_get_GROUP_nullable
functions.signature: static inline struct ofpact_group * ofpact_get_GROUP_nullable(const struct ofpact *ofpact)
functions.description: Nullable version of ofpact_get_GROUP with type assertion when non-null.
requirements: If non-null, type must be OFPACT_GROUP.

functions.name: ofpact_init_GROUP
functions.signature: static inline void ofpact_init_GROUP(struct ofpact_group *ofpact)
functions.description: Initializes a struct ofpact_group header.
requirements: Writable memory of sizeof(struct ofpact_group).

functions.name: ofpact_finish_GROUP
functions.signature: static inline void ofpact_finish_GROUP(struct ofpbuf *ofpbuf, struct ofpact_group **ofpactp)
functions.description: Pads and finalizes a GROUP action.
requirements: ofpbuf contains the action; *ofpactp is a valid GROUP action pointer.

functions.name: ofpact_put_CONTROLLER
functions.signature: static inline struct ofpact_controller * ofpact_put_CONTROLLER(struct ofpbuf *ofpacts)
functions.description: Appends and initializes a CONTROLLER action with space for header; user data is variable-length and follows the header.
requirements: ofpacts must be a valid ofpbuf.
If adding userdata, append bytes then call ofpact_finish_CONTROLLER to finalize length.

functions.name: ofpact_get_CONTROLLER
functions.signature: static inline struct ofpact_controller * ofpact_get_CONTROLLER(const struct ofpact *ofpact)
functions.description: Casts to struct ofpact_controller after asserting type is OFPACT_CONTROLLER.
requirements: ofpact must be type OFPACT_CONTROLLER.

functions.name: ofpact_get_CONTROLLER_nullable
functions.signature: static inline struct ofpact_controller * ofpact_get_CONTROLLER_nullable(const struct ofpact *ofpact)
functions.description: Nullable version of ofpact_get_CONTROLLER.
requirements: If non-null, type must be OFPACT_CONTROLLER.

functions.name: ofpact_init_CONTROLLER
functions.signature: static inline void ofpact_init_CONTROLLER(struct ofpact_controller *ofpact)
functions.description: Initializes a CONTROLLER action header.
requirements: Writable memory for struct ofpact_controller.

functions.name: ofpact_finish_CONTROLLER
functions.signature: static inline void ofpact_finish_CONTROLLER(struct ofpbuf *ofpbuf, struct ofpact_controller **ofpactp)
functions.description: Finalizes a CONTROLLER action after any userdata has been appended.
requirements: ofpbuf contains the action; update pointer after finish.

functions.name: ofpact_put_ENQUEUE
functions.signature: static inline struct ofpact_enqueue * ofpact_put_ENQUEUE(struct ofpbuf *ofpacts)
functions.description: Appends and initializes an ENQUEUE action.
requirements: ofpacts must be valid. Caller must set port and queue.

functions.name: ofpact_get_ENQUEUE
functions.signature: static inline struct ofpact_enqueue * ofpact_get_ENQUEUE(const struct ofpact *ofpact)
functions.description: Casts to struct ofpact_enqueue after asserting type is OFPACT_ENQUEUE.
requirements: ofpact must be OFPACT_ENQUEUE.

functions.name: ofpact_get_ENQUEUE_nullable
functions.signature: static inline struct ofpact_enqueue * ofpact_get_ENQUEUE_nullable(const struct ofpact *ofpact)
functions.description: Nullable version of ofpact_get_ENQUEUE.
requirements: If non-null, type must be OFPACT_ENQUEUE.

functions.name: ofpact_init_ENQUEUE
functions.signature: static inline void ofpact_init_ENQUEUE(struct ofpact_enqueue *ofpact)
functions.description: Initializes an ENQUEUE action header.

functions.description: Helper to append and compose a SET_FIELD (or REG_LOAD) with given field, value, and optional mask, writing into ofpacts.
requirements: ofpacts must be valid and initialized.
Field pointer must be a valid mf_field.
value points to at least field->n_bytes of data; mask, if non-null, must be at least field->n_bytes.
Caller should finish the action via returned pointer being fully composed by this helper.

functions.name: ofpact_put_reg_load

functions.name: ofpact_put_reg_load2
functions.signature: struct ofpact_set_field *ofpact_put_reg_load2(struct ofpbuf *ofpacts, const struct mf_field *, const void *value, const void *mask);
functions.description: Variant helper to compose a REG_LOAD-like action. Exact differences from ofpact_put_reg_load are not documented here.
requirements: Same as ofpact_put_set_field.
Semantics vs reg_load are unknown in this header; caller should consult implementation.

functions.name: ovs_instruction_name_from_type
functions.signature: const char *ovs_instruction_name_from_type(enum ovs_instruction_type type);
functions.description: Returns the textual name for the given internal OVS instruction type.
requirements: type must be a valid enum ovs_instruction_type.

functions.name: ovs_instruction_type_from_name
functions.signature: int ovs_instruction_type_from_name(const char *name);
functions.description: Returns the enum value of an OVS instruction type for a given name, or a negative/error code if not found. Exact return conventions not documented here.
requirements: name must be a non-null C string.

functions.name: ovs_instruction_type_from_ofpact_type
functions.signature: enum ovs_instruction_type ovs_instruction_type_from_ofpact_type(enum ofpact_type, enum ofp_version);
functions.description: Maps an ofpact action type and protocol version to the corresponding OVS instruction type, if applicable.
requirements: ofpact_type and version must be valid values.

functions.name: ovs_instruction_type_from_inst_type
functions.signature: enum ofperr ovs_instruction_type_from_inst_type(enum ovs_instruction_type *instruction_type, const uint16_t inst_type);
functions.description: Translates a raw OpenFlow instruction type (inst_type) to an internal ovs_instruction_type, storing it at instruction_type. Returns ofperr.
requirements: instruction_type must be a non-null output pointer.
inst_type must be a valid OpenFlow instruction type field.
Caller must check returned enum ofperr.

functions.signature: ovs_be32 ovsinst_bitmap_to_openflow(uint32_t ovsinst_bitmap, enum ofp_version);
functions.description: Converts an internal instruction capability bitmap to an OpenFlow instruction bitmap for the given version.
requirements: ovsinst_bitmap must be a valid internal bitmask.
Version must be valid.

functions.name: ovsinst_bitmap_from_openflow
functions.signature: uint32_t ovsinst_bitmap_from_openflow(ovs_be32 ofpit_bitmap, enum ofp_version);
functions.description: Converts an OpenFlow instruction bitmap to the internal instruction capability bitmap for the given version.
requirements: ofpit_bitmap must be an OpenFlow-formatted instruction bitmap.
Version must be valid.

functions.name: ofpraw_decode
functions.signature: enum ofperr ofpraw_decode(enum ofpraw *raw, const struct ofp_header *oh)
functions.description: Parses an OpenFlow message header and determines its raw message identifier (OFPRAW_*). Returns an OpenFlow error code (0 on success) and stores the decoded value in 'raw'. Typically used to validate message length against the expected body format for that raw type.
requirements: raw must be a non-null pointer to receive the decoded value.
oh must point to a valid, fully formed OpenFlow message header (and underlying message) in network byte order.
On invalid or unsupported message/type/length, the function returns a nonzero enum ofperr; callers should check the return value before using 'raw'.
The message length must be valid for the decoded type; otherwise an OFPERR (e.g., OFPERR_OFPBRC_BAD_LEN) is returned.

functions.name: ofpraw_decode_assert
functions.signature: enum ofpraw ofpraw_decode_assert(const struct ofp_header *oh)
functions.description: Decodes an OpenFlow message header into an OFPRAW_* value, asserting internally that decoding succeeds. This is a convenience for callers that expect 'oh' to be valid and want a direct enum ofpraw result.
requirements: oh must point to a valid, fully formed OpenFlow message header (and underlying message) whose type/length is decodable.
If the header is invalid, this function will abort/trigger an assertion failure (behavior implied by name). Only use when message validity is guaranteed.

functions.name: ofpraw_pull
functions.signature: enum ofperr ofpraw_pull(enum ofpraw *raw, struct ofpbuf *msg)
functions.description: Parses and removes ("pulls") the OpenFlow header from 'msg', decodes it to an OFPRAW_* value, and returns 0 on success or an error code on failure. Useful when progressively parsing a message payload after consuming headers.
requirements: raw must be non-null to receive the decoded value.
msg must be a non-null, initialized ofpbuf whose data begins with a complete OpenFlow header and message.
On error, the return value is nonzero (enum ofperr) and 'msg' contents should be considered not advanced; callers must check the return value before using 'raw' or the remaining buffer.

functions.name: ofpraw_pull_assert
functions.signature: enum ofpraw ofpraw_pull_assert(struct ofpbuf *msg)
functions.description: Like ofpraw_pull() but asserts that the buffer contains a valid decodable OpenFlow message, returning the OFPRAW_* value and removing the header from 'msg'. Intended for contexts where message validity is guaranteed.
requirements: msg must be a non-null, initialized ofpbuf whose data begins with a complete, valid OpenFlow message.
On invalid message data, the function will abort/trigger an assertion failure (behavior implied by name).

functions.name: ofpraw_decode_partial
functions.signature: enum ofperr ofpraw_decode_partial(enum ofpraw *raw, const struct ofp_header *oh, size_t length)
functions.description: Decodes an OpenFlow header into an OFPRAW_* value using only 'length' bytes available from 'oh'. This is for cases where only a partial buffer is present; performs length validation against the expected format for the decoded type.
requirements: raw must be non-null to receive the decoded value.
oh must point to the start of an OpenFlow header.
length must specify the number of contiguous bytes available starting at 'oh'. If insufficient for a valid header/body, a nonzero enum ofperr is returned.
Callers must check the return value before using 'raw'.

functions.name: ofpraw_alloc
functions.signature: struct ofpbuf *ofpraw_alloc(enum ofpraw raw, uint8_t ofp_version, size_t extra_tailroom)
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new ofpbuf pre-initialized with an OpenFlow header for the given raw message type and protocol version, reserving 'extra_tailroom' bytes for payload growth.
requirements: raw must specify a message type valid for 'ofp_version'.
ofp_version must be a valid OpenFlow version supported by the raw type.
extra_tailroom may be any size; allocation can fail only via system allocation failure (returned pointer will be NULL in such cases depending on allocator semantics).
Caller takes ownership of the returned ofpbuf and must free it per ofpbuf lifecycle.

functions.name: ofpraw_alloc_xid
functions.signature: struct ofpbuf *ofpraw_alloc_xid(enum ofpraw raw, uint8_t ofp_version, ovs_be32 xid, size_t extra_tailroom)
functions.description: Allocates a new ofpbuf with an OpenFlow header for the specified raw message type and version, initializing the transaction ID (xid) field to 'xid'. Reserves 'extra_tailroom' for the payload.
requirements: raw must be valid for 'ofp_version'.
xid is provided in network byte order (ovs_be32).
Caller must free the returned buffer per ofpbuf lifecycle.
On allocation failure, a NULL may be returned (allocator dependent).

functions.name: ofpraw_alloc_reply
functions.signature: struct ofpbuf *ofpraw_alloc_reply(enum ofpraw raw, const struct ofp_header *request, size_t extra_tailroom)
functions.description: Allocates a new ofpbuf containing a reply OpenFlow header for the given 'raw' reply type, matching the version and xid from the provided 'request'. Reserves 'extra_tailroom' bytes for body data.
requirements: raw must be an appropriate reply type for the 'request' message.
request must point to a valid OpenFlow request header whose version/xid can be copied.
Caller assumes ownership of the returned ofpbuf and must free it.
Callers should ensure the reply body matches the reply type’s expected format/length before sending.

functions.name: ofpraw_alloc_stats_reply
functions.signature: struct ofpbuf *ofpraw_alloc_stats_reply(const struct ofp_header *request, size_t extra_tailroom)
functions.description: Allocates a new ofpbuf initialized as a multipart/statistics reply corresponding to the provided multipart request, matching version and xid. Reserves 'extra_tailroom' for the reply body.
requirements: request must be a valid multipart/statistics request header.
If 'request' is not a statistics request, behavior is undefined or an error may be produced during later processing; callers must only pass a stats request.
Caller must free the returned ofpbuf per ofpbuf lifecycle.

functions.name: ofpraw_put
functions.signature: void ofpraw_put(enum ofpraw raw, uint8_t ofp_version, struct ofpbuf *out)
functions.description: Appends an OpenFlow header for the specified raw type and version to the provided ofpbuf.
requirements: out must be a non-null, initialized ofpbuf with enough space (or ability to grow) to append the header.
raw must be valid for 'ofp_version'.
Caller is responsible for appending any required body fields to match the message format and for updating length if needed (or later calling ofpmsg_update_length).

functions.name: ofpraw_put_xid
functions.signature: void ofpraw_put_xid(enum ofpraw raw, uint8_t ofp_version, ovs_be32 xid, struct ofpbuf *out)
functions.description: Appends an OpenFlow header for the provided raw type and version to 'out', initializing the transaction ID to 'xid'.
requirements: out must be a non-null, initialized ofpbuf.
raw must be valid for 'ofp_version'.
xid must be in network byte order (ovs_be32).
Caller must append a body consistent with the message type and handle final length.

functions.name: ofpraw_put_reply
functions.signature: void ofpraw_put_reply(enum ofpraw raw, const struct ofp_header *request, struct ofpbuf *out)
functions.description: Appends a reply header for the specified reply type to 'out', matching version and xid from 'request'.
requirements: out must be a non-null, initialized ofpbuf.
request must be a valid OpenFlow request header.
raw must be the correct reply type for the request kind.
Caller must append the appropriate body and finalize message length.

functions.name: ofpraw_put_stats_reply
functions.signature: void ofpraw_put_stats_reply(const struct ofp_header *request, struct ofpbuf *out)
functions.description: Appends a multipart/statistics reply header to 'out', matching version and xid from the provided multipart request header.
requirements: out must be a non-null, initialized ofpbuf.
request must be a valid multipart/statistics request header.
Caller must append stats reply body segments and finalize length; may need to set multipart flags where applicable.

functions.name: ofpraw_get_name
functions.signature: const char *ofpraw_get_name(enum ofpraw raw)
functions.description: Returns a constant, human-readable name string for the specified OFPRAW_* value. Useful for logging and diagnostics.
requirements: raw must be a valid OFPRAW_* value; otherwise the returned name may be a generic or implementation-defined placeholder.

functions.name: ofpraw_stats_request_to_reply
functions.signature: enum ofpraw ofpraw_stats_request_to_reply(enum ofpraw request_raw, uint8_t version)
functions.description: Maps a stats/multipart request OFPRAW_* value to the corresponding reply OFPRAW_* value for a given OpenFlow version. Use to select the correct reply type when constructing responses.
requirements: request_raw must be an OFPRAW_* that represents a statistics/multipart request.
version must be a valid OpenFlow version that supports the mapping; otherwise the returned value may be an undefined/invalid raw id.

functions.name: ofptype_decode
functions.signature: enum ofperr ofptype_decode(enum ofptype *type, const struct ofp_header *oh)
functions.description: Decodes an OpenFlow message header into a semantic message type (OFPTYPE_*), abstracting version/vendor differences. Returns 0 on success and stores the decoded type in 'type'.
requirements: type must be a non-null pointer to receive the result.
oh must point to a valid, fully formed OpenFlow message header (and message).
Callers must check the enum ofperr return value before using '*type'.

functions.name: ofptype_pull
functions.signature: enum ofperr ofptype_pull(enum ofptype *type, struct ofpbuf *msg)
functions.description: Parses and removes the OpenFlow header from 'msg' and decodes it into an OFPTYPE_* value. Returns 0 on success or an error code on failure.
requirements: type must be non-null to receive the decoded value.
msg must be an initialized ofpbuf whose data begins with a valid OpenFlow message.
On nonzero return, callers must not assume the buffer was advanced or that '*type' is valid.

functions.name: ofptype_from_ofpraw
functions.signature: enum ofptype ofptype_from_ofpraw(enum ofpraw raw)
functions.description: Maps a raw message identifier (OFPRAW_*) to its semantic message type (OFPTYPE_*).
requirements: raw must be a valid OFPRAW_* value; otherwise the result may be an unspecified OFPTYPE_* or a special/implementation-defined value.

functions.name: ofptype_get_name
functions.signature: const char *ofptype_get_name(enum ofptype type)
functions.description: Returns a constant, human-readable name string for a given semantic message type (OFPTYPE_*).
requirements: type should be a valid OFPTYPE_* value; otherwise the returned string may be a generic placeholder.

functions.name: ofpmsg_update_length
functions.signature: void ofpmsg_update_length(struct ofpbuf *msg)
functions.description: Updates the length field in the OpenFlow header at the start of 'msg' to match the current size of the buffer. Call after constructing or appending to a message.
requirements: msg must be a non-null, initialized ofpbuf that begins with an OpenFlow header.
The buffer must contain at least a full header; otherwise behavior is undefined.

functions.name: ofpmsg_body
functions.signature: const void *ofpmsg_body(const struct ofp_header *oh)
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the start of the OpenFlow message body that follows the headers represented by 'oh', abstracting header variations across versions/extensions.
requirements: oh must point to a valid OpenFlow message header in memory large enough to cover its header.
The returned pointer is only valid as long as the underlying message storage remains valid.

functions.name: ofpmsg_is_stat_request
functions.signature: bool ofpmsg_is_stat_request(const struct ofp_header *oh)
functions.description: Returns true if 'oh' represents a statistics (multipart) request message.
requirements: oh must point to a valid OpenFlow message header.
Caller should not assume anything about the body beyond this classification.

functions.name: ofpmsg_is_stat_reply
functions.signature: bool ofpmsg_is_stat_reply(const struct ofp_header *oh)
functions.description: Returns true if 'oh' represents a statistics (multipart) reply message.
requirements: oh must point to a valid OpenFlow message header.

functions.name: ofpmsg_is_stat
functions.signature: bool ofpmsg_is_stat(const struct ofp_header *oh)
functions.description: Returns true if 'oh' is any statistics (multipart) message (either request or reply).
requirements: oh must point to a valid OpenFlow message header.

functions.name: ofpmp_init
functions.signature: void ofpmp_init(struct ovs_list *replies, const struct ofp_header *request)
functions.description: Initializes a list of ofpbufs to build a multipart/statistics reply corresponding to 'request'. The list will hold one or more parts that together form the reply.
requirements: replies must be a non-null pointer to an initialized ovs_list to be used as a container for reply parts.
request must be a valid OpenFlow request header; for stats usage, it should be a multipart request.

functions.name: ofpmp_reserve
functions.signature: struct ofpbuf *ofpmp_reserve(struct ovs_list *replies, size_t len)
functions.description: Ensures space for 'len' bytes in the current multipart reply part, allocating/starting a new part if necessary, and returns the ofpbuf for writing. Use when you need an ofpbuf handle for filling structured data.
requirements: replies must be a non-null, initialized list previously set up with ofpmp_init().
len is the number of bytes the caller intends to write next; must be consistent with the reply type’s expected layout.
Caller will write into the returned ofpbuf and later call ofpmsg_update_length as appropriate.

functions.name: ofpmp_append
functions.signature: void *ofpmp_append(struct ovs_list *replies, size_t len)
functions.description: Appends 'len' bytes to the multipart reply sequence and returns a pointer to the reserved writable space. Useful for directly writing variable-length payloads across parts.
requirements: replies must be a non-null, initialized list previously prepared by ofpmp_init().
len is the number of bytes to append; caller must fill exactly 'len' bytes.
Caller is responsible for ensuring message part boundaries and sizes remain within OpenFlow limits.

functions.name: ofpmp_postappend
functions.signature: void ofpmp_postappend(struct ovs_list *replies, size_t start_ofs)
functions.description: Performs any bookkeeping needed after the caller has written data starting at 'start_ofs' within the multipart reply sequence. Typically used to finalize lengths or backfill size fields.
requirements: replies must be a non-null, initialized list previously prepared by ofpmp_init().
start_ofs must be a valid offset within the multipart data produced so far; the caller must compute and pass a correct value.

functions.name: ofpmp_version
functions.signature: enum ofp_version ofpmp_version(struct ovs_list *replies)
functions.description: Returns the OpenFlow version being used for the multipart reply represented by 'replies'.
requirements: replies must reference a multipart reply list initialized with ofpmp_init().

functions.name: ofpmp_decode_raw
functions.signature: enum ofpraw ofpmp_decode_raw(struct ovs_list *replies)
functions.description: Returns the raw message identifier (OFPRAW_*) corresponding to the multipart reply being constructed in 'replies'.
requirements: replies must reference a multipart reply list initialized with ofpmp_init().

functions.name: ofpmp_flags
functions.signature: uint16_t ofpmp_flags(const struct ofp_header *oh)
functions.description: Extracts and returns the multipart flags field from the given OpenFlow message header (e.g., the 'more' flag for multi-part replies).
requirements: oh must point to a valid OpenFlow multipart message header that contains a flags field appropriate to its version.

functions.name: ofpmp_more
functions.signature: bool ofpmp_more(const struct ofp_header *oh)
functions.description: Returns true if the multipart 'more' flag is set in the given OpenFlow header, indicating additional parts follow.
requirements: oh must point to a valid OpenFlow multipart message header with a flags field.

functions.name: ofpmp_assembler_clear
functions.signature: void ofpmp_assembler_clear(struct hmap *assembler)
functions.description: Clears all state from a multipart request reassembler hmap, freeing any in-progress assemblies. Use when resetting or shutting down the assembler.
requirements: assembler must be a non-null pointer to an hmap used for reassembly and initialized by the caller’s hmap utilities.

functions.name: ofpmp_assembler_run
functions.signature: struct ofpbuf *ofpmp_assembler_run(struct hmap *assembler, long long int now)
functions.description: Processes the reassembly state for multipart requests as of time 'now' and returns a completed, reassembled request buffer if one becomes available; otherwise returns NULL. Intended to be called periodically or after feeding parts.
requirements: assembler must be a non-null pointer to an hmap dedicated to multipart request reassembly.
now is a monotonically increasing timestamp (time base chosen by the caller) used for timeouts/aging.
Returned ofpbuf, if non-NULL, is owned by the caller.

functions.name: ofpmp_assembler_wait
functions.signature: long long int ofpmp_assembler_wait(struct hmap *assembler)
functions.description: Returns the time at which the caller should next wake to service the multipart reassembler (e.g., the earliest deadline among in-progress assemblies).
requirements: assembler must be a non-null pointer to an hmap used for multipart reassembly.

functions.name: ofpmp_assembler_execute
functions.signature: enum ofperr ofpmp_assembler_execute(struct hmap *assembler, struct ofpbuf *msg, struct ovs_list *out, long long int now)
functions.description: Feeds a multipart request message part into the reassembler. On receiving a complete assembled request, appends it to 'out'. Returns 0 on success or an OpenFlow error code on failure.
requirements: assembler must be a non-null pointer to an hmap used for multipart request reassembly.
msg must be a non-null ofpbuf containing a single OpenFlow message (a part of a multipart request).
out must be a non-null, initialized ovs_list to receive any completed assembled request buffers.
now is a timestamp used for reassembly timeouts/aging.
Caller must check the enum ofperr return value and handle errors appropriately.

functions.name: ofpbuf_const_initializer
functions.signature: static inline struct ofpbuf ofpbuf_const_initializer(const void *data, uint32_t size)
functions.description: Returns a by-value initializer for an ofpbuf that references existing immutable data [data..data+size). Intended for inspecting pre-existing data without moving/reallocating it.
requirements: data may be NULL only if size is 0 (implied by typical usage; header does not explicitly state but functions assume data or size==0 elsewhere)

Caller must treat the buffer contents as read-only; underlying storage is not owned by ofpbuf (inferred from "inspect existing data, without moving it around or reallocating it, and generally without modifying it at all")

functions.name: ofpbuf_use_ds
functions.signature: void ofpbuf_use_ds(struct ofpbuf *, const struct ds *);
functions.description: Configures an ofpbuf to use the storage owned by a dynamic string (ds). Likely sets base/data/size to point into ds without taking ownership.
requirements: The ofpbuf* must be a valid pointer to an initialized struct to receive fields
The ds* must be valid and contain accessible backing storage
Ownership and lifetime of ds storage must outlive the ofpbuf usage (inferred)

functions.name: ofpbuf_use_stack

functions.name: ofpbuf_use_data

functions.name: ofpbuf_init

functions.name: ofpbuf_uninit

functions.name: ofpbuf_reinit
functions.signature: void ofpbuf_reinit(struct ofpbuf *, size_t);

functions.name: ofpbuf_new
functions.signature: struct ofpbuf *ofpbuf_new(size_t);

functions.name: ofpbuf_new_with_headroom
functions.signature: struct ofpbuf *ofpbuf_new_with_headroom(size_t, size_t headroom);

requirements: First size parameter is initial data capacity (not including headroom)
headroom is the number of unused bytes reserved before data

functions.name: ofpbuf_clone
functions.signature: struct ofpbuf *ofpbuf_clone(const struct ofpbuf *);

functions.name: ofpbuf_clone_with_headroom
functions.signature: struct ofpbuf *ofpbuf_clone_with_headroom(const struct ofpbuf *, size_t headroom);

headroom specifies minimum bytes before data in the clone
Caller must free with ofpbuf_delete

functions.name: ofpbuf_clone_data
functions.signature: struct ofpbuf *ofpbuf_clone_data(const void *, size_t);
functions.description: Allocates a new ofpbuf and copies the specified raw data into it.
requirements: Data pointer must be valid for size bytes (size may be 0)
Caller must free with ofpbuf_delete

functions.name: ofpbuf_clone_data_with_headroom
functions.signature: struct ofpbuf *ofpbuf_clone_data_with_headroom(const void *, size_t, size_t headroom);
functions.description: Allocates a new ofpbuf, copies the given data, and provides at least the specified headroom before the data.
requirements: Data pointer must be valid for size bytes (size may be 0)
headroom is reserved before the copied data
Caller must free with ofpbuf_delete

functions.name: ofpbuf_delete
functions.signature: static inline void ofpbuf_delete(struct ofpbuf *b)
functions.description: Frees memory that b points to (via ofpbuf_uninit) as well as the ofpbuf struct itself. Safe on NULL.
requirements: b may be NULL
If non-NULL, b must have been initialized/allocated appropriately

functions.name: ofpbuf_at
functions.signature: static inline void *ofpbuf_at(const struct ofpbuf *b, size_t offset, size_t size)
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the byte at offset within the used data if at least offset+size bytes are present; otherwise returns NULL.
requirements: b must be non-NULL and b->data valid when b->size>0
offset+size must be <= b->size to get non-NULL result

functions.name: ofpbuf_at_assert
functions.signature: static inline void *ofpbuf_at_assert(const struct ofpbuf *b, size_t offset, size_t size)
functions.description: Returns a pointer to byte at offset in b, asserting that b contains at least offset+size bytes of data.
requirements: offset+size must be <= b->size; otherwise program aborts via assertion
b->data must be non-NULL

functions.name: ofpbuf_tail
functions.signature: static inline void *ofpbuf_tail(const struct ofpbuf *b)
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the byte following the last used byte in b (the current tail), or NULL if no data and no data pointer.
requirements: If b->size>0 then b->data must be non-NULL (asserted)

functions.name: ofpbuf_end
functions.signature: static inline void *ofpbuf_end(const struct ofpbuf *b)
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the byte following the last allocated byte (end of capacity), or NULL if no allocation.
requirements: If b->allocated>0 then b->base must be non-NULL (asserted)

functions.name: ofpbuf_put_uninit
functions.signature: void *ofpbuf_put_uninit(struct ofpbuf *, size_t);
functions.description: Appends size bytes to the buffer, expanding if necessary, and returns a pointer to the uninitialized space for caller to fill.
requirements: ofpbuf* must be valid
size may be zero
Caller must initialize the returned memory before reading

functions.name: ofpbuf_put_zeros
functions.signature: void *ofpbuf_put_zeros(struct ofpbuf *, size_t);
functions.description: Appends size zero-initialized bytes to the buffer and returns a pointer to the start of the appended region.
requirements: ofpbuf* must be valid
size may be zero

functions.name: ofpbuf_put
functions.signature: void *ofpbuf_put(struct ofpbuf *, const void *, size_t);
functions.description: Appends size bytes copied from the given data pointer to the buffer and returns a pointer to the start of the appended region.
requirements: Source data pointer must be valid for size bytes (size may be 0)
ofpbuf* must be valid

functions.name: ofpbuf_put_hex
functions.signature: char *ofpbuf_put_hex(struct ofpbuf *, const char *s, size_t *n);
functions.description: Parses hex-encoded string s and appends the corresponding bytes to the buffer; returns pointer to the location where text parsing stopped. Also optionally stores number of bytes appended into n.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated or length-determinable string of hex; exact format unspecified
n may be NULL or a valid pointer to receive byte count

functions.name: ofpbuf_reserve
functions.signature: void ofpbuf_reserve(struct ofpbuf *, size_t);
functions.description: Reserves headroom at the beginning of the buffer by advancing data pointer without changing size, ensuring capacity as needed.
requirements: ofpbuf* must be valid
size specifies headroom to reserve (may be 0)

functions.name: ofpbuf_push_uninit
functions.signature: void *ofpbuf_push_uninit(struct ofpbuf *b, size_t);
functions.description: Prepends size bytes of uninitialized space before current data, growing if needed; returns pointer to the new space.
requirements: b must be valid
size may be 0
Caller must initialize the returned space before read

functions.name: ofpbuf_push_zeros
functions.signature: void *ofpbuf_push_zeros(struct ofpbuf *, size_t);
functions.description: Prepends size zeroed bytes to the front of the buffer and returns pointer to the new space.
requirements: ofpbuf* must be valid
size may be 0

functions.name: ofpbuf_push
functions.signature: void *ofpbuf_push(struct ofpbuf *b, const void *, size_t);
functions.description: Prepends size bytes copied from the given data pointer to the front of the buffer and returns pointer to the new space.
requirements: Source pointer must be valid for size bytes (size may be 0)
b must be valid

functions.name: ofpbuf_insert
functions.signature: void ofpbuf_insert(struct ofpbuf *b, size_t offset, const void *data, size_t);
functions.description: Inserts size bytes from data into buffer b at the given offset within the used data, moving existing data as needed.
requirements: b must be valid
offset must be <= current size (inferred typical behavior; exact constraint not stated)
data must be valid for size bytes when size>0

functions.name: ofpbuf_headroom
functions.signature: static inline size_t ofpbuf_headroom(const struct ofpbuf *b)
functions.description: Returns the number of unused bytes before the start of used data (headroom).
requirements: b->base and b->data must be valid pointers defining the buffer layout

functions.name: ofpbuf_tailroom
functions.signature: static inline size_t ofpbuf_tailroom(const struct ofpbuf *b)
functions.description: Returns the number of free bytes available to append at the tail without reallocation.
requirements: Relies on ofpbuf_end(b) and ofpbuf_tail(b) being valid; base/data/allocated/size must be consistent

functions.name: ofpbuf_msgsize
functions.signature: static inline size_t ofpbuf_msgsize(const struct ofpbuf *b)
functions.description: Returns number of bytes from b->msg to the current tail (used space starting from msg).
requirements: b->msg must be within [data, tail] for meaningful result (implied)
b must be valid

functions.name: ofpbuf_prealloc_headroom
functions.signature: void ofpbuf_prealloc_headroom(struct ofpbuf *, size_t);
functions.description: Ensures at least the specified headroom exists before data, reallocating and moving data if necessary.
requirements: ofpbuf* must be valid
size is required headroom in bytes

functions.name: ofpbuf_prealloc_tailroom
functions.signature: void ofpbuf_prealloc_tailroom(struct ofpbuf *, size_t);
functions.description: Ensures at least the specified tailroom exists after the used data, reallocating if necessary.
requirements: ofpbuf* must be valid
size is required tailroom in bytes

functions.name: ofpbuf_trim
functions.signature: void ofpbuf_trim(struct ofpbuf *);
functions.description: Shrinks any extra allocation so that capacity matches current size or otherwise trims unused space.
requirements: ofpbuf* must be valid

functions.name: ofpbuf_align
functions.signature: void ofpbuf_align(struct ofpbuf *);
functions.description: Adjusts data alignment within the buffer to satisfy required alignment constraints (e.g., for headers).
requirements: ofpbuf* must be valid
Exact alignment policy is unspecified here

functions.name: ofpbuf_padto
functions.signature: void ofpbuf_padto(struct ofpbuf *, size_t);
functions.description: Pads the buffer with zero bytes up to at least the given total size.
requirements: ofpbuf* must be valid
size is the minimum total size after padding

functions.name: ofpbuf_shift
functions.signature: void ofpbuf_shift(struct ofpbuf *, int);
functions.description: Shifts the data pointer and adjusts size by a signed amount, effectively adding/removing headroom or trimming from head.
requirements: ofpbuf* must be valid
Shift amount may be positive or negative; exact limits unspecified

functions.name: ofpbuf_clear
functions.signature: static inline void ofpbuf_clear(struct ofpbuf *b)
functions.description: Clears any data from b by resetting data to base and size to 0.
requirements: b must be valid; sets b->data=b->base and b->size=0

functions.name: ofpbuf_pull
functions.signature: static inline void *ofpbuf_pull(struct ofpbuf *b, size_t size)
functions.description: Removes size bytes from the head of b and returns a pointer to the first byte removed. Asserts that b contains at least size bytes.
requirements: b->size must be >= size; otherwise assertion failure
If size==0, returns current data pointer without modification

functions.name: ofpbuf_try_pull
functions.signature: static inline void *ofpbuf_try_pull(struct ofpbuf *b, size_t size)
functions.description: If b has at least size bytes, removes them from the head and returns the original data pointer; otherwise returns NULL and leaves b unchanged.
requirements: b must be valid
size may be 0

functions.name: ofpbuf_steal_data
functions.signature: void *ofpbuf_steal_data(struct ofpbuf *);
functions.description: Transfers ownership of the current data buffer out of the ofpbuf and returns a pointer to it, leaving the ofpbuf empty.
requirements: ofpbuf* must be valid
Caller becomes responsible for freeing the returned memory using the appropriate allocator

functions.name: ofpbuf_to_string
functions.signature: char *ofpbuf_to_string(const struct ofpbuf *, size_t maxbytes);
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated printable string representation of the buffer contents, limited to maxbytes of data.
requirements: ofpbuf* must be valid
Caller must free the returned string with free()

functions.name: ofpbuf_from_list
functions.signature: static inline struct ofpbuf *ofpbuf_from_list(const struct ovs_list *list)
functions.description: Returns the containing ofpbuf pointer given a pointer to its embedded list_node field (CONTAINER_OF).

functions.name: ofpbuf_equal

If size>0, data pointers must be valid for memcmp

functions.name: ofpbuf_oversized

ofpbuf_tail(ofpacts) must be valid

functions.name: ofpbuf_headersize
functions.signature: static inline size_t ofpbuf_headersize(const struct ofpbuf *b)
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes from b->header to b->msg (the header length).
requirements: b->header and b->msg must be set such that msg >= header

functions.name: ofpbuf_truncate
functions.signature: static inline void ofpbuf_truncate(struct ofpbuf *b, size_t new_size)
functions.description: Truncates the buffer to new_size bytes from the tail end, asserting that current size >= new_size.
requirements: b->size must be >= new_size; otherwise assertion failure

functions.name: ovs_list_init
functions.signature: void ovs_list_init(struct ovs_list *list)
functions.description: Initializes a list head or element to the empty self-referential state. Typical usage: call on a list head before any insertions, or on an element to reset its links.

Must be called before using 'list' as a list head or after the element is no longer linked into any list.

functions.name: ovs_list_poison
functions.signature: void ovs_list_poison(struct ovs_list *list)
functions.description: Sets list pointers to a recognizable invalid (poison) state to help catch misuse in debugging. Not for production traversal or dereference.
requirements: list must be a valid, writable pointer to struct ovs_list.
Code must not dereference or traverse a poisoned list; it is intended only for debugging visibility.

functions.name: ovs_list_insert
functions.signature: void ovs_list_insert(struct ovs_list *before, struct ovs_list *elem)
functions.description: Inserts elem just before the node 'before' in its list. Commonly used with a list head to insert at a defined position.

requirements: first and last must denote a valid, possibly empty half-open range within the same source list, where walking via next from first up to (but not including) last is valid.
before must be a valid node currently linked into the destination list (which may be the same list).
All pointers must be non-null and writable for the nodes being re-linked.

functions.name: ovs_list_push_front
functions.signature: void ovs_list_push_front(struct ovs_list *list, struct ovs_list *elem)
functions.description: Inserts elem at the beginning (front) of list.

elem must be a valid node not currently linked into any list.
Pointers must be non-null and writable.

functions.name: ovs_list_push_back
functions.signature: void ovs_list_push_back(struct ovs_list *list, struct ovs_list *elem)
functions.description: Inserts elem at the end (back) of list.
requirements: list must be a valid list head currently initialized and linked to itself if empty.
elem must be a valid node not currently linked into any list.
Pointers must be non-null and writable.

functions.name: ovs_list_replace
functions.signature: void ovs_list_replace(struct ovs_list *element, const struct ovs_list *position)
functions.description: Replaces the node at 'position' with 'element'. After the call, 'position' is detached and 'element' occupies its former place.
requirements: position must be a valid node currently linked into a list.
element must be a valid node not currently linked into any list.
position must be non-null and may be const as it is not modified; element must be writable.

functions.name: ovs_list_moved
functions.signature: void ovs_list_moved(struct ovs_list *list, const struct ovs_list *orig)
functions.description: Repairs neighbor pointers after 'list' has been moved in memory (e.g., via realloc), given its original address 'orig'. If 'list' was a list head, leaves it as head; otherwise fixes neighbors to point to the new address.
requirements: list must contain the moved struct ovs_list now residing at a new address.

Pointers must be valid; 'orig' may point to freed memory but is not dereferenced.

functions.name: ovs_list_move
functions.signature: void ovs_list_move(struct ovs_list *dst, struct ovs_list *src)
functions.description: Copies the link fields from src to dst and then fixes links as if the list head was moved from src to dst. Effectively makes dst the new head of the same list that src headed.

dst must be a valid, writable struct ovs_list storage not currently linked into a list.

functions.name: ovs_list_remove
functions.signature: struct ovs_list *ovs_list_remove(struct ovs_list *elem)
functions.description: Removes elem from its current list and returns the element that followed it in that list.
requirements: Undefined behavior if elem is not currently linked into a list.
elem must be a valid, writable pointer to a linked node.
The returned pointer is valid only as long as the list remains intact; caller must handle possible end-of-list (it may be the list head).

functions.name: ovs_list_pop_front
functions.signature: struct ovs_list *ovs_list_pop_front(struct ovs_list *list)
functions.description: Removes and returns the front element of list.

list must be a valid list head.

functions.name: ovs_list_pop_back
functions.signature: struct ovs_list *ovs_list_pop_back(struct ovs_list *list)
functions.description: Removes and returns the back element of list.
requirements: Undefined behavior if list is empty before removal.
list must be a valid list head.
Returned pointer is the removed node; caller owns it for further operations.

functions.name: ovs_list_front

functions.name: ovs_list_back

requirements: list_ must be a valid list head and must not be empty.
Caller must not pass an empty list.

functions.name: ovs_list_size
functions.signature: size_t ovs_list_size(const struct ovs_list *list)
functions.description: Counts and returns the number of elements in list. Runs in O(n).

functions.name: ovs_list_is_empty
functions.signature: bool ovs_list_is_empty(const struct ovs_list *list)
functions.description: Returns true if list has no elements; false otherwise.
requirements: list must be a valid list head initialized to point to itself if empty.

functions.name: ovs_list_is_singleton
functions.signature: bool ovs_list_is_singleton(const struct ovs_list *list)
functions.description: Returns true if list has exactly one element; false otherwise.
requirements: list must be a valid list head.
Depends on list links being well-formed (circular).

functions.name: ovs_list_is_short
functions.signature: bool ovs_list_is_short(const struct ovs_list *list)
functions.description: Returns true if list has 0 or 1 elements; false otherwise.
requirements: list must be a valid list head.
Depends on list links being well-formed (circular).

functions.name: ovs_list_push_back_all
functions.signature: void ovs_list_push_back_all(struct ovs_list *dst, struct ovs_list *src)

Lists must be well-formed before the call.

functions.description: Returns the hash value stored in a given hmap_node. Useful when comparing or debugging nodes within a hash map.
