functions.name: hmap_node_is_null
functions.signature: static inline bool hmap_node_is_null(const struct hmap_node *node)
functions.description: Checks whether a node has been marked as null via hmap_node_nullify(). Indicates that the node is not currently inserted into an hmap since insertion un-nullifies it.

functions.name: hmap_node_nullify
functions.signature: static inline void hmap_node_nullify(struct hmap_node *node)
functions.description: Marks a node with a distinctive next-pointer value that can later be tested with hmap_node_is_null(). This is a sentinel mark; insertion into an hmap will clear it.

: calling this will overwrite node->next.

functions.name: hmap_init
functions.signature: void hmap_init(struct hmap *);
functions.description: Initializes an hmap to an empty state. Must be called before any other operations on the map.

Call before any insertion or capacity adjustments.

functions.name: hmap_destroy

functions.name: hmap_clear
functions.signature: void hmap_clear(struct hmap *);

requirements: The hmap argument must be a valid pointer to an initialized struct hmap.

functions.name: hmap_swap
functions.signature: void hmap_swap(struct hmap *a, struct hmap *b);
functions.description: Swaps the contents (buckets, size, etc.) of two hmaps.
requirements: a and b must be valid pointers to initialized struct hmap objects.

functions.name: hmap_moved
functions.signature: void hmap_moved(struct hmap *hmap);
functions.description: Notifies the implementation that the struct hmap object has been relocated in memory, allowing it to fix internal self-referential pointers (e.g., buckets pointing to &one when mask == 0).
requirements: hmap must be a valid pointer to an initialized struct hmap.
Call after moving/relocating the struct hmap in memory (e.g., via struct assignment or relocation).

functions.name: hmap_count
functions.signature: static inline size_t hmap_count(const struct hmap *hmap)
functions.description: Returns the number of nodes currently stored in the hmap.
requirements: hmap must be a valid pointer to a struct hmap (initialization implied).

functions.name: hmap_is_empty
functions.signature: static inline bool hmap_is_empty(const struct hmap *hmap)
functions.description: Returns true if the map contains no nodes. Note: This function is documented as thread-safe even if other hmap operations are not.
requirements: hmap must be a valid pointer to a struct hmap.

functions.name: hmap_expand_at
functions.signature: void hmap_expand_at(struct hmap *, const char *where);

where should point to a string literal or otherwise valid C-string for logging (may be produced by OVS_SOURCE_LOCATOR).

No return value; callers should not expect error reporting other than internal assertions/logging.

functions.name: hmap_shrink_at
functions.signature: void hmap_shrink_at(struct hmap *, const char *where);
functions.description: Shrinks the hash map capacity, if possible, to reduce overhead while maintaining performance. The where parameter is used for debug logging.
requirements: The hmap argument must be a valid pointer to an initialized struct hmap.
where should point to a valid C-string for logging (e.g., OVS_SOURCE_LOCATOR).

functions.name: hmap_shrink
functions.signature: void hmap_shrink(struct hmap *hmap);
functions.description: Potentially shrinks the hash map’s bucket array to reduce memory usage when the table is underutilized, while keeping reasonable lookup performance. This is a convenience macro that calls hmap_shrink_at(hmap, OVS_SOURCE_LOCATOR) to record the call site for debugging.
requirements: hmap must be initialized via hmap_init() or an appropriate initializer before calling.
The map should be in a consistent state (no concurrent modification without external synchronization).
No return value; callers should not expect error reporting other than internal assertions/logging.

functions.name: hmap_reserve_at
functions.signature: void hmap_reserve_at(struct hmap *, size_t capacity, const char *where);
functions.description: Ensures the hash map has at least the requested capacity, potentially resizing to accommodate capacity nodes efficiently. The where parameter is used for debug logging.
requirements: The hmap argument must be a valid pointer to an initialized struct hmap.
capacity is a size_t specifying desired capacity.
where should point to a valid C-string for logging.

functions.name: hmap_reserve
functions.signature: void hmap_reserve(struct hmap *hmap, size_t capacity);
functions.description: Ensures the hash map has capacity for approximately the specified number of nodes, potentially reallocating and rehashing the bucket array. This is a convenience macro that calls hmap_reserve_at(hmap, capacity, OVS_SOURCE_LOCATOR) to record the call site for debugging.
requirements: hmap must be initialized via hmap_init() or an appropriate initializer before calling.
capacity is a size_t specifying the desired capacity; must be a valid nonnegative size_t value (0 is allowed but may result in no expansion).
The map should be in a consistent state (no concurrent modification without external synchronization).
No return value; callers should not expect error reporting other than internal assertions/logging.

functions.name: hmap_insert_at
functions.signature: static inline void hmap_insert_at(struct hmap *hmap, struct hmap_node *node, size_t hash, const char *where)
functions.description: Inserts node with the given hash into the map and, if load suggests, expands the map to maintain performance. The where parameter is used for debug logging.
requirements: hmap must be a valid pointer to an initialized struct hmap.
node must be a valid pointer to an hmap_node that is not currently linked into any hmap (its fields will be overwritten).
hash must be the computed hash for the object containing node.
where should be a valid C-string for logging.
Caller should not concurrently modify the same hmap without external synchronization.

functions.name: hmap_insert
functions.signature: void hmap_insert(struct hmap *hmap, struct hmap_node *node, size_t hash);
functions.description: Inserts node into the hash map with the given precomputed hash value, expanding the map if needed to maintain performance. This is a convenience macro that calls hmap_insert_at(hmap, node, hash, OVS_SOURCE_LOCATOR) to record the call site for debugging. Use when adding a new element that embeds an hmap_node.
requirements: hmap must be initialized via hmap_init() or an appropriate initializer before calling.
node must be a valid pointer to an embedded struct hmap_node within a longer-lived object; its lifetime must outlive its membership in the map.
node must not already be in any hmap (inserting the same node twice into a map or into two maps is invalid).
hash must be the intended hash for the object; the same hash must be used for subsequent lookups that rely on hash comparisons.
This function may expand the map; callers should not hold pointers into the bucket array across this call.
Not thread-safe without external synchronization; avoid concurrent modification while calling.
No return value; callers should not expect error reporting other than internal assertions/logging.

functions.name: hmap_insert_fast
functions.signature: static inline void hmap_insert_fast(struct hmap *hmap, struct hmap_node *node, size_t hash)
functions.description: Inserts node with the given hash into the map without automatically expanding capacity. Useful when batch-inserting or when the caller manages capacity separately.
requirements: hmap must be a valid pointer to an initialized struct hmap.
node must be a valid pointer to an hmap_node that is not currently linked into any hmap (its fields will be overwritten).
hash must be the computed hash for the object containing node.
Does not expand the table; caller may call hmap_expand[_at]() separately if needed.

functions.name: hmap_remove
functions.signature: static inline void hmap_remove(struct hmap *hmap, struct hmap_node *node)
functions.description: Removes node from the map. Does not shrink the table automatically.
requirements: hmap must be a valid pointer to an initialized struct hmap.
node must be a valid pointer to an hmap_node that is currently present in hmap; otherwise removal will fail or corrupt the structure.
After removal, the caller must not use node->next as a list link for this map unless reinserted.
If shrinking is desired, caller should invoke hmap_shrink[_at]().

functions.name: hmap_node_moved
functions.signature: void hmap_node_moved(struct hmap *, struct hmap_node *, struct hmap_node *);
functions.description: Notifies that a node currently in the map has been moved to a new memory address (e.g., its enclosing object was relocated). Updates internal bucket linkage to point to the new node address without changing ordering.
requirements: The hmap argument must be a valid pointer to an initialized struct hmap.
The second argument (old node) must be the exact node pointer currently stored in the map.
The third argument (new node) must be the new address for that same logical node and must represent the same hash value as the old node.
Should be used when the node's address changes but its membership and hash do not.

functions.name: hmap_replace
functions.signature: static inline void hmap_replace(struct hmap *hmap, const struct hmap_node *old_node, struct hmap_node *new_node)
functions.description: Replaces old_node in-place with new_node within the same map and bucket chain. The new_node must hash to the same value; links are preserved, and old_node is detached for the caller to free or reuse.
requirements: hmap must be a valid pointer to an initialized struct hmap.
old_node must be currently present in hmap.
new_node must be a valid pointer and must hash to the same value as old_node (explicitly required).
Caller is responsible for ensuring any higher-level invariants (e.g., key uniqueness) are maintained after replacement.
After the call, old_node is no longer part of the map and must not be used as if linked.

functions.name: hmap_random_node
functions.signature: struct hmap_node *hmap_random_node(const struct hmap *);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a randomly selected node from the map, or NULL if the map is empty. Useful for sampling.
requirements: hmap must be a valid pointer to an initialized struct hmap.

functions.name: hmap_first_with_hash
functions.signature: static inline struct hmap_node *hmap_first_with_hash(const struct hmap *hmap, size_t hash)
functions.description: Returns the first node in the map with the given hash value, or NULL if none exists.
requirements: hmap must be a valid pointer to an initialized struct hmap.
hash is evaluated once and should be the computed hash for the search key.

functions.name: hmap_next_with_hash
functions.signature: static inline struct hmap_node *hmap_next_with_hash(const struct hmap_node *node)
functions.description: Given a node previously found in a hash bucket, returns the next node in the same map with the same hash value, or NULL if none remain.
requirements: node must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an hmap_node currently or previously in a bucket chain.
The node must have a valid hash field (set during insertion).
Do not call with NULL; use hmap_first_with_hash() to start a scan.

functions.name: hmap_first_in_bucket
functions.signature: static inline struct hmap_node *hmap_first_in_bucket(const struct hmap *hmap, size_t hash)
functions.description: Returns the first node in the bucket that the provided hash would select, or NULL if the bucket is empty.
requirements: hmap must be a valid pointer to an initialized struct hmap.
hash is evaluated once and used only for bucket selection.

functions.name: hmap_next_in_bucket
functions.signature: static inline struct hmap_node *hmap_next_in_bucket(const struct hmap_node *node)
functions.description: Returns the next node in the same bucket as the provided node, or NULL if there is none. May skip or miss nodes if the map was reallocated since node was visited.
requirements: node must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an hmap_node.

functions.name: hmap_contains
functions.signature: bool hmap_contains(const struct hmap *, const struct hmap_node *);
functions.description: Returns true if the given node is currently contained in the specified hmap, false otherwise.
requirements: The hmap argument must be a valid pointer to an initialized struct hmap.
The node pointer should be a valid hmap_node pointer (may be NULL depending on implementation, but behavior for NULL is unspecified in this header).

functions.name: hmap_first
functions.signature: static inline struct hmap_node *hmap_first(const struct hmap *hmap)
functions.description: Returns the first node in the map in an arbitrary order, or NULL if the map is empty.
requirements: hmap must be a valid pointer to an initialized struct hmap.

functions.name: hmap_next
functions.signature: static inline struct hmap_node *hmap_next(const struct hmap *hmap, const struct hmap_node *node)
functions.description: Returns the next node in the map following node, in arbitrary order, or NULL if node is the last element. Reallocation may cause nodes to be skipped or visited twice. Removal of node does not prevent calling this function (node->next is preserved), but freeing node does.
requirements: hmap must be a valid pointer to an initialized struct hmap.
node must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an hmap_node obtained from iteration over hmap and must not have been freed.

functions.name: hmap_at_position
functions.signature: struct hmap_node *hmap_at_position(const struct hmap *, struct hmap_position *);
functions.description: Fetches the node at the iterator position specified by hmap_position and updates the position to the next element. Supports external iteration across buckets with saved state.
requirements: The hmap argument must be a valid pointer to an initialized struct hmap.
The position argument must be a valid pointer to a struct hmap_position with fields bucket and offset initialized appropriately for the desired starting point.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: UTF-8 C string without embedded NUL, terminated by a single NUL.
# We generate a single bytes blob containing many NUL-terminated strings to seed
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() calls across stubs.

ASCII_SAFE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_:. /,[]{}()@#%+~=\"'"

KNOWN_LEVELS = ["off", "emer", "err", "warn", "info", "dbg"]
KNOWN_DESTS = ["SYSLOG", "CONSOLE", "FILE"]

# Valid snippets for OVS ofpacts and instruction parsers.
ACTIONS_SNIPPETS = [
    "output:1",
    "drop",
    "set_field:1->in_port",
    "set_field:aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff->eth_src",
    "push_vlan:0x8100,set_field:100->vlan_vid",
    "controller(reason=no_match,max_len=128)",
    "resubmit(,1)",
    "group:5",
    "meter:1",
    "learn(table=2,hard_timeout=10,priority=100,load:0x1->NXM_NX_REG0[])",
    "ct(commit,table=1)",
]

INSTRUCTION_SNIPPETS = [
    "apply_actions(output:2)",
    "write_actions(pop_vlan)",
    "clear_actions",
    "goto_table:3",
]

# JSON-friendly strings for constructors and object puts.
JSON_STRINGS = [
    "",            # empty string
    "hello",
    "Open vSwitch",
    "προγραμμα",
    "line1\\nline2",
    "\"quoted\"",
    "🚀 rocket",
]

# Filenames for vlog_set_log_file and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
FILENAMES = [
    "log.txt",
    "tmp/log-001.txt",
    "var/log/ovs/test.log",
    "dev/null.log",
]

# Patterns and methods for vlog.
PATTERNS = [
    "%D %T|%p|%m",
    "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S|%u|%c|%m",
]
SYSLOG_METHODS = [
    "native:localhost",
    "udp:127.0.0.1:514",
    "file:/var/log/ovs-syslog.log",
]

# Helper to generate a random printable utf-8 string of bounded length without NULs.
def rand_printable(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(ASCII_SAFE) for _ in range(n))

# Helper to pick with bias towards known-good values but still randomize.
def pick_weighted(rng: random.Random, known: List[str]) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return rng.choice(known)
    return rand_printable(rng, 0, 24)

# Compose multiple NUL-terminated C-strings into one bytes blob.
def pack_cstrings(parts: List[str]) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for p in parts:
        # Ensure no embedded NULs; replace any accidental ones with space.
        p = p.replace('\x00', ' ')
        out.extend(p.encode('utf-8', errors='strict'))
        out.append(0)
    return bytes(out)

# Build a corpus list of strings in an order that benefits the stubs.
def build_segments(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    segs: List[str] = []

    # Program name and version used by ovs_set_program_name.
    segs.append(pick_weighted(rng, ["ovs-vswitchd", "ovsdb-server", "test-prog"]))
    segs.append(pick_weighted(rng, ["3.2.0", "2.17.0", "1.0", rand_printable(rng, 1, 8)]))

    # JSON creators consume general strings.
    segs.extend(rng.sample(JSON_STRINGS, k=min(len(JSON_STRINGS), 5)))
    segs.append(rand_printable(rng, 0, 64))

    # Extra strings for JSON value coverage.
    segs.append("value-" + rand_printable(rng, 3, 12))

    # VLOG parsing: levels and destinations.
    segs.extend(KNOWN_LEVELS)
    segs.extend(KNOWN_DESTS)
    segs.append(pick_weighted(rng, ["info:ANY", "warn:console:pattern", "dbg"]))

    # Verbosity, patterns, syslog method/target.
    segs.append(pick_weighted(rng, ["any:info", "module:dbg", "dbg:dbg"]))
    segs.extend(PATTERNS)
    segs.extend(SYSLOG_METHODS)
    segs.append(pick_weighted(rng, ["127.0.0.1:514", "/dev/log", "localhost"]))

    # ofpacts_parse_actions and instructions: provide both valid and random.
    segs.extend(ACTIONS_SNIPPETS)
    segs.append(','.join(rng.sample(ACTIONS_SNIPPETS, k=rng.randint(1, min(4, len(ACTIONS_SNIPPETS))))))
    segs.extend(INSTRUCTION_SNIPPETS)
    segs.append(','.join(rng.sample(INSTRUCTION_SNIPPETS, k=rng.randint(1, min(3, len(INSTRUCTION_SNIPPETS))))))

    # ovs_instruction_type_from_name: try known names and random.
    segs.extend(["apply_actions", "write_actions", "clear_actions", "goto_table"])
    segs.append(rand_printable(rng, 0, 20))

    # hmap_* stubs use where strings; keep short debug labels.
    segs.extend([
        "expand@fuzz", "shrink@fuzz", "reserve@fuzz",
        "insert@fuzz-" + str(rng.randint(0, 1000))
    ])

    # Filenames for vlog_set_log_file and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
    segs.extend(FILENAMES)

    # Additional random payloads for vlog_direct_write_to_log_file_unsafe and general use.
    for _ in range(4):
        segs.append(rand_printable(rng, 0, 128))

    return segs


def truncate_corpus(blob: bytes, maxlen: int = 4096) -> bytes:
    if len(blob) <= maxlen:
        return blob
    # Find the last NUL before the limit to keep whole strings.
    cut = blob.rfind(b"\x00", 0, maxlen)
    if cut == -1:
        # Fallback: ensure at least one full C-string ends within limit.
        return blob[:maxlen - 1] + b"\x00"
    return blob[:cut + 1]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    segs = build_segments(rng)
    blob = pack_cstrings(segs)
    blob = truncate_corpus(blob, 4096)
    return blob

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator targets a variety of consumers that read arbitrary bytes:
# - JSON streaming parser (expects UTF-8 JSON snippets; may be partial)
# - OpenFlow action/instruction parsers (expects binary OpenFlow action blobs)
# - ofpbuf utilities (operate on arbitrary byte data)
# - vlog file paths (handled via FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME, not this buffer)
#
# Strategy: Produce a bytes buffer that is likely valid and interesting for both
# JSON parsers and OpenFlow action/instruction parsers by composing segments:
# 1) A valid, small JSON text (ensures json_parser_* can often complete)
# 2) A small random complete JSON object/array variant to diversify
# 3) A compact OpenFlow-like action header sequence with plausible fields
# 4) A mix of aligned big-endian integers and random payload to feed ofpbuf tests
# The overall size is kept <= 1024 bytes.

JSON_EXAMPLES: List[str] = [
    "null",
    "true",
    "false",
    "0",
    "1",
    "-1",
    "3.14159",
    "\"\"",
    "\"ovs\"",
    "[]",
    "[1,2,3]",
    "{}",
    "{\"a\":1}",
    "{\"k\":\"v\"}",
    "{\"arr\":[1,2,{\"x\":true}],\"n\":null}",
]

# Helper to build a plausible OpenFlow action list (binary). We do not aim to be
# exhaustive, just to provide well-formed lengths and recognizable patterns for
# multiple versions. Many OpenFlow actions are 8-byte aligned with a 4-byte header
# in Open vSwitch ofpact internal representation, but wire actions have their own
# format. We'll emit a mixture of plausible OpenFlow 1.3 action headers and payloads
# with correct length fields to exercise parsers len checking paths.

def ofp_action_output(port: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # OpenFlow 1.3 ofp_action_output: type=0 (OFPAT_OUTPUT), len=16
    # struct: type(2), len(2), port(4), max_len(2), pad(6)
    typ = 0  # OFPAT_OUTPUT
    length = 16
    b = struct.pack(
        ">HHIH",
        typ,
        length,
        port & 0xFFFFFFFF,
        max_len & 0xFFFF,
    )
    # pad 6 bytes
    return b + b"\x00" * 6


def ofp_action_set_vlan_vid(vlan: int) -> bytes:
    # OFPAT_SET_VLAN_VID (type=1), len=8, vlan_vid(2), pad(2), pad(4)
    typ = 1
    length = 8
    b = struct.pack(
        ">HHH",
        typ,
        length,
        vlan & 0x0FFF,
    )
    # pad 2 + 4
    return b + b"\x00" * 6


def ofp_action_set_vlan_pcp(pcp: int) -> bytes:
    # OFPAT_SET_VLAN_PCP (type=2), len=8, pcp(1), pad(3), pad(4)
    typ = 2
    length = 8
    b = struct.pack(
        ">HHB",
        typ,
        length,
        pcp & 0x07,
    )
    # pad 3 + 4
    return b + b"\x00" * 7


def ofp_action_set_queue(queue: int) -> bytes:
    # OFPAT_SET_QUEUE (type=21 in OF1.2/1.3), len=8, queue_id(4)
    typ = 21
    length = 8
    b = struct.pack(
        ">HHI",
        typ,
        length,
        queue & 0xFFFFFFFF,
    )
    return b


def ofp_action_set_nw_tos(tos: int) -> bytes:
    # OFPAT_SET_NW_TOS (type=5 in OF1.0/1.1; len=8), tos(1), pad(3), pad(4)
    typ = 5
    length = 8
    b = struct.pack(
        ">HHB",
        typ,
        length,
        tos & 0xFF,
    )
    return b + b"\x00" * 7


def ofp_action_group(group_id: int) -> bytes:
    # OF1.1+ experimental: OFPAT_GROUP type=22 len=8, group(4)
    typ = 22
    length = 8
    return struct.pack(
        ">HHI",
        typ,
        length,
        group_id & 0xFFFFFFFF,
    )


def build_openflow_actions(rng: random.Random, budget: int) -> bytes:
    actions = []
    # create 1..5 actions
    count = rng.randint(1, 5)
    for _ in range(count):
        choice = rng.randint(0, 5)
        if choice == 0:
            actions.append(ofp_action_output(rng.randint(1, 65535), rng.choice([0, 128, 512, 0xFFFF])))
        elif choice == 1:
            actions.append(ofp_action_set_vlan_vid(rng.randint(1, 4094)))
        elif choice == 2:
            actions.append(ofp_action_set_vlan_pcp(rng.randint(0, 7)))
        elif choice == 3:
            actions.append(ofp_action_set_queue(rng.randint(0, 2**32 - 1)))
        elif choice == 4:
            actions.append(ofp_action_set_nw_tos(rng.randint(0, 255)))
        else:
            actions.append(ofp_action_group(rng.randint(0, 2**32 - 1)))
        if sum(len(a) for a in actions) >= budget:
            break
    blob = b"".join(actions)
    # Ensure even minimal padding to align to 8 bytes if needed
    if len(blob) % 8:
        blob += b"\x00" * (8 - (len(blob) % 8))
    return blob[:budget]


def build_json_snippet(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose a base JSON value and optionally wrap in an array/object or whitespace
    base = rng.choice(JSON_EXAMPLES)
    # Optionally embed base in a simple object/array with small strings
    variants = []
    variants.append(base)
    variants.append("[" + base + "]")
    variants.append("{\"k\":" + base + "}")
    variants.append("\n  " + base + "  \n")
    # Maybe add a small string with escapes
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        s = ''.join(chr(rng.randint(32, 126)) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 8)))
        esc = s.replace('\\', '\\\\').replace('"', '\\"')
        variants.append("{\"s\":\"" + esc + "\",\"v\":" + base + "}")
    txt = rng.choice(variants)
    # Ensure length <= 256 suitable for fuzzers
    if len(txt) > 256:
        txt = txt[:256]
    return txt.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')


def be32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">I", x & 0xFFFFFFFF)

def be16(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">H", x & 0xFFFF)

def be64(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">Q", x & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)


def build_aligned_payload(rng: random.Random, budget: int) -> bytes:
    parts = []
    # Mix of BE16/32/64 and small random chunks; helps ofpbuf consumers
    count = rng.randint(4, 12)
    for _ in range(count):
        t = rng.randint(0, 4)
        if t == 0:
            parts.append(be16(rng.getrandbits(16)))
        elif t == 1:
            parts.append(be32(rng.getrandbits(32)))
        elif t == 2:
            parts.append(be64(rng.getrandbits(64)))
        elif t == 3:
            n = rng.randint(0, 16)
            parts.append(rng.randbytes(n))
        else:
            # MAC-like 6 bytes
            mac = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(6))
            parts.append(mac)
        if sum(len(p) for p in parts) >= budget:
            break
    blob = b"".join(parts)
    return blob[:budget]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Budget within 256..1024 to match stub truncations and allow OpenFlow blobs
    total_budget = rng.randint(256, 1024)

    # 1) JSON snippet (up to 200 bytes)
    json_part = build_json_snippet(rng)
    json_part = json_part[: min(len(json_part), 200)]

    # 2) Another JSON or newline separator to encourage parser completion
    json_part2 = b"\n" + build_json_snippet(rng)

    used = len(json_part) + len(json_part2)
    remaining = max(0, total_budget - used)

    # 3) OpenFlow actions blob (aim ~40% of remaining)
    of_budget = int(remaining * 0.4)
    of_budget = max(32, min(of_budget, 512)) if remaining >= 32 else 0
    of_blob = build_openflow_actions(rng, of_budget) if of_budget > 0 else b""

    # 4) Aligned payload for ofpbuf paths fills the rest
    remaining = max(0, total_budget - (used + len(of_blob)))
    aligned_blob = build_aligned_payload(rng, remaining)

    out = json_part + json_part2 + of_blob + aligned_blob
    # Safety clamp to 4096
    return out[:4096]

def make_large_array(n):
    return "[" + ",".join(str(i) for i in range(n)) + "]"

def make_large_object(n):

    for i in range(n):

        elif i % 5 == 1:

        elif i % 5 == 2:

        elif i % 5 == 3:

        else:
            v = "[1,2,3]"
        parts.append(json.dumps("k" + str(i)) + ":" + v)
    return "{" + ",".join(parts) + "}"

        parts.append(rng.choice(DIR_NAMES))
        # Sometimes include a dotted hidden-like dir
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            parts[-1] = "." + parts[-1]
    base = rand_name(rng)
    # Occasionally use typical names
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        base = rng.choice(["in", "input", "data", "payload", "case"]) + ("-" + rand_name(rng,1,4) if rng.random()<0.5 else "")
    ext = rng.choice(EXTS)
    fn = "/".join(parts + [base + ext]) if parts else base + ext
    return fn


def pick_json(rng):
    # Mix from base snippets and larger ones, but cap size to <= 3800 bytes to ensure
    # room for filename and separator.
    choice_pool = JSON_SNIPPETS[:]
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        choice_pool += LARGE_JSONS
    doc = rng.choice(choice_pool)
    # Optionally wrap in whitespace to simulate typical pretty cases.
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        ws_left = "\n" * rng.randint(0, 2) + " " * rng.randint(0, 4)
        ws_right = " " * rng.randint(0, 4) + "\n" * rng.randint(0, 2)
        doc = ws_left + doc + ws_right
    # Ensure size limit
    b = doc.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > 3800:
        # Trim arrays/objects deterministically but keeping valid JSON
        if doc.startswith("[") and doc.endswith("]"):
            # Keep first N elements
            elems = doc[1:-1].split(",")
            keep = max(1, 3800 // 6)
            doc = "[" + ",".join(elems[:keep]) + "]"
        elif doc.startswith("{") and doc.endswith("}"):
            items = doc[1:-1].split(",")
            keep = max(1, 3800 // 12)
            doc = "{" + ",".join(items[:keep]) + "}"
        else:
            doc = doc[:3800]
    return doc


def assemble_buffer(filename: str, json_text: str) -> bytes:
    # Combine as: filename NUL json
    buf = filename.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore') + b"\x00" + json_text.encode('utf-8')
    # Enforce global cap
    return buf[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    filename = build_filename(rng)
    json_text = pick_json(rng)
    return assemble_buffer(filename, json_text)
